vt_talus_field_boulders.blurb: Talus Field Boulders is a cluster of seventeen boulder problems in central Vermont, a few minutes' drive from Middlebury and a very short walk above the neighbouring Trailside blocks. The grades cover nearly the whole range: a handful of easy V0 to V2 warm-ups, a solid middle of V3 to V5, and several hard problems into the V7 to V9 bracket. The blocks sit at the foot of a talus slope, so landings are uneven and a lot of pads are needed, and footing between boulders takes care. The wider Abbey Pond zone is known for being shady, damp and buggy, so pick a dry, cool day.

vt_breadloaf.blurb: Breadloaf is a single sizeable gneiss boulder in the Shipyard sector of Bromley Forest, in southern Vermont, set beside a powerline clearing in the woods above the road. It holds seventeen problems that run from the very easiest up to a hard V8, with most of the lines landing between V2 and V5. The climbing is dynamic and slopey, with some slab problems too, and it makes a good stop for a mixed group. Because the forest sits close to a busy highway, expect some road noise from the boulders.

vt_crash_site.blurb: Crash Site is a boulder zone in the Mothership section of Bromley Forest, in southern Vermont, where the dense gneiss is known for quality lines. One large central boulder anchors it, with smaller blocks scattered on either side, and you can slip through the gap between the two halves of the big block. Of its seventeen problems, most fall from VB to V3, with a few much harder ones around V8 and V10. It sits high in the woods, a hike up a logging road and past a cairn from the log landing, and the nearby highway makes it a little noisy.

va_bears_den_boulders.blurb: Bears Den Boulders is a small set of seventeen problems below the Bears Den overlook near Bluemont in northern Virginia, on a ridge that looks west across the Shenandoah Valley. It is a gentle place to boulder: the problems are mostly low to the ground, about ten of them at V1, with the rest reaching up to V5. A worn path leads down either side of the ledge to the blocks beneath it. Expect plenty of hikers wandering the overlook above, particularly on fine weekends, and a short, easy approach from the parking at the trail center.

va_bird_s_nest.blurb: Bird's Nest is a popular crag at Great Falls on the Potomac, set beside the river trail a short way downstream of the Canal Cut. It holds seventeen climbs, mostly top-rope lines with a smaller number of trad routes and one scramble, and it has some of the longest climbs in the park. The grades start at easy 5.7 and 5.8 and pile up around 5.10 to 5.11, with a couple of 5.12s for the strong. Several lines are rated as if led, so top-ropers may find them a touch easier than the number suggests.

va_jungle_block.blurb: Jungle Block is a single boulder with a short roof near its top, in the Center Lightside sector of Guest River Gorge near Coeburn in southwest Virginia. The gorge is a rail-to-trail corridor along the river, and most of its climbing is reached through an old coal train tunnel. The block carries seventeen problems, mostly V3 to V5 with a few easier ones below and one problem near V6. Bring pads, and expect a patch of briars around the clearing.
